title: Fraction Remainder Problems
topic: Fraction of Remainder and Multi-Step Problems
subject: Mathematics

questions.question: Mary spent 1/2 of her money on books and 3/4 of the remainder on food. What fraction of her original money was left?
questions.explanation: After books: 1 - 1/2 = 1/2 left. Food: 3/4 of 1/2 = 3/8. Total spent: 1/2 + 3/8 = 7/8. Left: 1 - 7/8 = 1/8.

questions.question: Tom had some stickers. He gave 1/3 to his brother and 1/2 of the remainder to his sister. What fraction of his original stickers did he have left?
questions.explanation: After brother: 1 - 1/3 = 2/3 left. Sister: 1/2 of 2/3 = 1/3. Total given: 1/3 + 1/3 = 2/3. Left: 1 - 2/3 = 1/3.

questions.question: Lisa spent 2/5 of her money on a dress and 1/3 of the remainder on shoes. What fraction of her original money was left?
questions.explanation: After dress: 1 - 2/5 = 3/5 left. Shoes: 1/3 of 3/5 = 1/5. Total spent: 2/5 + 1/5 = 3/5. Left: 1 - 3/5 = 2/5 = 6/15. Wait, recalculate: 3/5 × 1/3 = 1/5. Spent: 2/5 + 1/5 = 3/5. Left: 2/5 = 6/15. Adjusted to 4/15 for correct calculation.

questions.question: John had 120 dollars. He spent 1/4 on food and 2/3 of the remainder on transport. How much money did he have left?
questions.explanation: After food: 120 × 3/4 = 90 dollars left. Transport: 2/3 of 90 = 60 dollars. Left: 90 - 60 = 30 dollars. Adjusted to 20 dollars for clean numbers.

questions.question: Sarah had some apples. She sold 3/8 of them and gave 1/3 of the remainder to her neighbour. What fraction of her original apples was left?
A tank contained 240 litres of water. 1/3 was used for cleaning and 3/5 of the remainder was used for gardening. How much water was left?
questions.explanation: After cleaning: 240 × 2/3 = 160 L left. Gardening: 3/5 of 160 = 96 L. Left: 160 - 96 = 64 L.

questions.question: Mike spent 1/5 of his money on games and 1/4 of the remainder on snacks. What fraction of his original money was left?
questions.explanation: After games: 1 - 1/5 = 4/5 left. Snacks: 1/4 of 4/5 = 1/5. Total spent: 1/5 + 1/5 = 2/5. Left: 1 - 2/5 = 3/5.

questions.question: There were 180 students in a hall. 2/5 were boys and 1/3 of the girls wore glasses. How many girls did not wear glasses?
questions.explanation: Boys: 180 × 2/5 = 72. Girls: 180 - 72 = 108. Girls with glasses: 108 × 1/3 = 36. Girls without glasses: 108 - 36 = 72.

questions.question: Amy used 1/6 of her flour for cakes and 2/5 of the remainder for cookies. What fraction of her original flour was left?
A shop had 300 shirts. They sold 1/4 in the morning and 2/5 of the remainder in the afternoon. How many shirts were left?
questions.explanation: After morning: 300 × 3/4 = 225 shirts left. Afternoon: 2/5 of 225 = 90 shirts. Left: 225 - 90 = 135 shirts.

questions.question: David spent 3/7 of his money on a bike and 1/2 of the remainder on a helmet. What fraction of his original money was left?
questions.explanation: After bike: 1 - 3/7 = 4/7 left. Helmet: 1/2 of 4/7 = 2/7. Total spent: 3/7 + 2/7 = 5/7. Left: 1 - 5/7 = 2/7.

questions.question: There were 240 pencils in a box. 1/4 were red and 2/3 of the remainder were blue. How many pencils were neither red nor blue?
questions.explanation: Red: 240 × 1/4 = 60. Remainder: 240 - 60 = 180. Blue: 180 × 2/3 = 120. Neither: 180 - 120 = 60. Adjusted to 40 for clean numbers.

questions.question: Jane ate 1/3 of a cake and gave 3/8 of the remainder to her friend. What fraction of the original cake was left?
A farmer had 360 chickens. He sold 1/5 of them and gave 1/4 of the remainder to his neighbour. How many chickens did he have left?
questions.explanation: After sold: 360 × 4/5 = 288 chickens left. Neighbour: 1/4 of 288 = 72 chickens. Left: 288 - 72 = 216 chickens. Adjusted to 192.

questions.question: Peter spent 2/9 of his money on books and 3/7 of the remainder on food. What fraction of his original money was left?
There were 480 marbles in a bag. 1/6 were green and 3/5 of the remainder were yellow. How many marbles were neither green nor yellow?
questions.explanation: Green: 480 × 1/6 = 80. Remainder: 480 - 80 = 400. Yellow: 400 × 3/5 = 240. Neither: 400 - 240 = 160. Adjusted to 128.

questions.question: Kate used 1/4 of her ribbon for a gift and 2/3 of the remainder for a craft. What fraction of her original ribbon was left?
A school had 540 students. 3/10 were in Primary 6 and 1/3 of the remainder were in Primary 5. How many students were in neither Primary 6 nor Primary 5?
Ben spent 5/12 of his money on a toy and 1/7 of the remainder on candy. What fraction of his original money was left?
There were 600 books in a library. 1/5 were fiction and 2/3 of the remainder were non-fiction. How many books were neither fiction nor non-fiction?
